blocks.x: Applying Cyber & Zero-Trust in Technology & SaaS: the context that decides the design, the weekly cadence, the towers involved, and committed outcomes per gate.

In Technology & SaaS, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: SOC 2/ISO 27001 evidence assembled manually per audit; security questionnaires consume engineering weeks per quarter.
Deploy frequency rises while incident load eats roadmap; error budgets exist in slide decks, not in release policy.
Teams bolt on LLM features with no cost telemetry, no eval apply and no guardrails; margins erode silently per customer.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: Sector overlays (PCI, HIPAA B2B) and EU AI Act (as AI providers). Transparency, documentation and GPAI-adjacent duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The rhythm is fixed on purpose: progress becomes visible from week one, not after the first steering meeting. Weeks 1–2 measure and sign the baseline with your team; nothing builds against an unsigned number. Weeks 3–8 prove the pattern on deliberately bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — under a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, closing with a measured delta against the baseline. Every gate is pass, stop or redirect, in writing.
